messages.content: write a story about a child who thinks his aunt does not want to read with him, but learns she was making a place for him.

a child brings his book to his aunt. before he can ask his question, she stands up and moves her chair away from the window. he thinks she is leaving, so he puts the book down. she asks why he looks sad. he says that he wanted them to read together. she says that she moved the chair to make room for him next to her. she gets another chair, and he brings his book back. now they can both see the page without either person having to stand.
keep only the sentence where she gives her reason.
she says that she moved the chair to make room for him next to her.
what did the child see, and what did he think was happening?
he saw his aunt stand up and move her chair. he thought that she was leaving. he did not yet know that she wanted to make room for him.
explain that in fewer words.
he saw her move the chair and thought she was leaving. later, she told him why she moved it.
what could he ask before putting the book down?
could we read together now, or do you need to leave?
ask just about reading.
could we read together now?
i wrote a message last night saying i will see you tomorrow. i did not send it. now it is morning, and the meeting is today. what should i change?
change tomorrow to today before sending it. the time word should work for the day when the other person reads your message, rather than only the day when you first wrote it.
write the changed message.
i will see you today.
we are meeting at the library after lunch. add that.
i will see you at the library after lunch today.
can you make it a question that asks whether the plan is still good?
are we still meeting at the library after lunch today?
my friend says yes, but asks whether i can bring the book. i can. write my reply.
yes, i can bring the book. i will see you after lunch.
what detail about the book is still not in this conversation?
we do not know its name or what it is about. we only know that your friend asked you to bring it and you said you can.
what is the difference between i read to my neighbor and i read about my neighbor?
in the first sentence, your neighbor listens to your reading. in the other, your neighbor is the person the writing is about.
explain that with fewer words.
read to is about reading for someone to hear. read about is about who or what is in the writing.
write a small story using the first idea.

a man visits his neighbor in the afternoon. she has a book she enjoys, but she would like someone to read with her. he reads a few pages while she listens. then they talk about what happened in the story. he asks if she wants another page, and she says that they can keep the next part for tomorrow.
does the story say she cannot read?
no. it says that she wants someone to read with her. that does not tell us whether she can read herself.
now use the other idea in just one sentence.
i read a story in the paper about my neighbor and her garden.
keep the same meaning, but put in the paper at the start.
in the paper, i read a story about my neighbor and her garden.
my friend sent me a picture they are drawing. it is not finished, and they asked what i think.
you can say what you see and ask about what they want to do next. if you know something you like in it, name that part rather than saying you like everything.
i like the tree but do not understand the empty part on the left.
you could write: i like the tree. what do you want to put in the empty part on the left?
they say that part will stay empty. i thought every part had to be full.
an empty part can be a choice. your friend may want more room around the tree or may like how the picture looks that way. you can ask what they like about leaving it empty.
write that as a question for them.
what do you like about keeping that part empty?
if they ask what i would do, can i give a different idea without saying theirs is wrong?
yes. you could say: i might put a small flower there, but i understand that you want to keep the space around the tree.
keep the first part only.
i might put a small flower there.
i stopped reading a book last month and want to start again. i do not remember every person in it.
you could read the last few pages you finished before reading more. if that is not enough, go back to the start of the part you were reading. you do not have to begin the whole book again right away.
say that in fewer words.
read the last few pages you finished. that may help you remember enough to read more.
i left a note saying stopped when the girl came to the village. how can that help?
it gives you a part of the story to look for. you can find the part where the girl comes to the village, then read a little before it to remember the context.
write only the words from my note.
stopped when the girl came to the village.
can you write a better note for next time without knowing the page number?
stopped at the part where the girl came to the village. begin a little before that when returning to the book.
why a little before?
reading the part before the place where you stopped can help bring back what was happening when you left the story.
i am waiting for my friend at a lunch table. someone asks whether the chair next to me is free. i want to keep it for my friend.
you could say: i am waiting for a friend. could i keep this chair for them, please?
does that say for sure that my friend has already chosen that chair?
no. it says you want to keep the chair for your friend. it does not say your friend already chose it.
can you make it shorter?
i am waiting for a friend. could i keep this chair for them, please?
what if there are no other chairs?
you could check whether your friend is close and ask how to make room for everyone. what works best may change with the place and the needs of the people there.
give me a simple reply that does not choose for everyone.
i am waiting for a friend, but i see there is no other chair. can we work out a way for everyone to sit?
does that say my friend has already come?
no. it still says that you are waiting.
write a short story where we know where a book is, but the child in the story does not.

a child leaves her book on a chair before going to the kitchen. while she is away, her father moves it to the shelf to make room for someone to sit. when she comes back, she looks at the chair and thinks the book is lost. she goes under the table to look for it. her father comes into the room and asks what she is trying to find.
where do we think she will look first?
the chair, because that is where she left it. she does not know that her father moved it.
ask my question in fewer words.
where will she look first?
why do we know the book is on the shelf?
the story told us that her father put it there while she was away. we know that part even though the child does not.
finish with the father helping her, but not making her feel wrong for asking.
he says: i moved your book to the shelf. i should have told you. she looks there and finds it. he gives it back, and she sits down to read.
did she lose the book outside?
no. it stayed in the room. she only did not know where it had been moved.
my sister and i both chose the quiet room. does that mean we wanted the same thing?
not always. you may have chosen the same room for different reasons. one person could want to read, while another wants to rest.
i wanted to draw, and she wanted to make a phone call where she could hear clearly.
then you chose the same room for different things. the quiet helped with both, but it was not the whole reason each of you chose it.
what if her call makes it hard for me to draw?
you could tell her that you need quiet too and ask how to use the room in a way that works for both of you. you might use it one after the other, or choose different places.
say that last part simply.
you might use the room one after the other, or find different places to do your work.
can you give me a message to say to her?
could we use this room one after the other? i want quiet for drawing, and your call needs a quiet place too.
does that say she cannot make the call?
no. it asks you both to choose how to use the room.
i wrote she wants to go home, then changed it to she wanted to go home. what changed?
wants can be about what she wants now. wanted is about what she wanted before now. the rest of the story helps make the time clear.
explain the difference in fewer words.
wants can be about now. wanted is about the past.
write two short story sentences using wanted and went.
she wanted to go home after the long day. she put her book away and went to the door.
does went to the door say she got home?
no. it only says she went to the door. it does not say whether she left or got home.
ask my last question with fewer words.
did she get home?
add a last sentence that says she did get home.
later that evening, she got home and sat down with her family.
i want to send a message, but i have not told you who it is for. what should you ask?
who is the message for, and what do you want it to say?
it is for a friend. i want to ask for my book back, but i do not know whether they finished it.
you could write: have you finished the book? when do you think you can return it?
can you keep just the part about when they can return it?
when do you think you can return the book?
what if they say they have not started yet?
you can choose whether to leave it with them longer or ask for it back. the message does not need to say that you are sad or that they did something wrong.
help me ask for it back with a kind message.
could i have the book back for now? you can read it another time if you would still like to.
can you explain my request simply?
you wanted a kind message asking for the book back.
we had music on while talking, then turned it off and kept talking. can you write that in one sentence?
we talked with music playing, then turned it off and kept talking.
did turning it off end the conversation?
no. your sentence says that the conversation went on after the music stopped.
make a small story about two friends doing that in a kitchen.
two friends sit in a kitchen with music on the radio. one cannot hear the conversation clearly. the other stops the music. they keep talking, and one reads a short line from the book.
make it simple and short.
two friends turn off the radio so they can hear each other. then they keep talking about a book.
why did the music stop in that story?
one friend could not hear the conversation clearly. they stopped the music so they could talk.
now let the music stop because the song finished, not because anyone chose to stop it.
two friends talk in a kitchen while a song plays. when the song is over, they keep talking. nobody stops it.

make this story short without changing why the girl leaves. a girl is reading in a room. she can hear her father call from the kitchen. she puts her book on the chair and goes to see what he needs. he asks her to bring two cups to the table.
a girl leaves her book to answer her father when he calls from the kitchen. he asks her to bring two cups to the table.
can you make it shorter still?
a girl answers her father when he calls, and he asks her to bring two cups.
did the original story say she brought the cups, or only that he asked?
it only said that he asked her. we do not know whether she brought the cups after that.
keep the shorter story, but put the book back in it.
a girl leaves her book to answer her father when he calls, and he asks her to bring two cups.
can you also say where she left the book?
a girl leaves her book on a chair to answer her father when he calls, and he asks her to bring two cups.
where was the book left in the original story?
on the chair.
